examples.en: My uncle came home on leave wearing his military uniform.

examples.ko: 이 가게에서는 군복 무늬 옷을 많이 팔아요.
examples.en: This shop sells a lot of clothes with a camouflage pattern.
He looked very sharp in his military uniform.

examples.ko: 아빠는 옛날 군복을 아직 옷장에 보관하세요.
examples.en: My dad still keeps his old military uniform in the closet.

examples.ko: 영화 속 배우들이 진짜 같은 군복을 입고 나왔어요.
examples.en: The actors in the movie appeared in realistic military uniforms.

examples.ko: 군복은 색깔이 어두워서 숲에서 눈에 잘 안 띄어요.
examples.en: Military uniforms are dark, so they're hard to spot in a forest.

explain: 군인이 입는 옷을 말하고, 경찰이나 소방관의 옷은 '제복'이라고 해요. 한국에서는 군복 무늬를 일상복이나 가방에 쓰는 일도 많아요. 훈련 때 입는 옷은 '전투복'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is the clothing soldiers wear; clothing for police or firefighters is called 제복. In Korea, the camouflage pattern is often used on everyday clothes and bags. The outfit worn in training is also called 전투복.

examples.en: I hurt my thigh while running.
My thigh muscles are knotted and sore.
The thigh part is the tastiest part of the chicken.
My thighs feel tight when I climb stairs.
I fell and got a bruise on my thigh.
Try doing thigh exercises regularly.

explain: 무릎 위쪽 다리 부분을 말하며 일상에서는 '허벅지'를 더 자주 말해요. 닭이나 돼지 요리 이야기에서도 나와요. 무릎 아래쪽은 '종아리'예요.
explain_en: It refers to the part of the leg above the knee, and in daily talk '허벅지' is heard more often. It also comes up when talking about chicken or pork dishes. The part below the knee is '종아리'.

examples.en: My arm stings when I get a shot.
My throat stung, so I took medicine.

examples.ko: 상처에 약을 바르면 조금 따끔할 거예요.
examples.en: It will sting a little when you put medicine on the wound.
My eyes stung and watered.
The teacher gave a stern word.
I was pricked by a needle and my finger stung.

explain: 주사, 소독약, 가시처럼 짧고 찌르는 듯한 아픔에 써요. 오래 계속되는 아픔은 '쑤시다', '욱신거리다'를 써요. '따끔하게 말하다'는 아프도록 엄하게 꾸짖는다는 비유로도 써요.
explain_en: It is for a short, sharp sting from a shot, antiseptic or a thorn. For a lasting ache, use 쑤시다 or 욱신거리다. 따끔하게 말하다 is also used figuratively for scolding someone sharply.

examples.ko: 겨울 산에 갈 때는 방한복을 꼭 입으세요.
examples.en: Be sure to wear cold-weather gear when you go to the mountains in winter.
The winter gear is thick, so it's hard to move around.
I was surprised that the winter gear cost more than I expected.

examples.ko: 방한복 안에 얇은 옷을 여러 겹 입었어요.
examples.en: I wore several thin layers under my winter gear.
I bought winter gear for the child as well.
This winter gear stays warm even at minus twenty degrees.

explain: 그냥 '겨울옷'이라고 하면 일반적인 두꺼운 옷이고, 방한복은 등산, 야외 활동, 현장 작업처럼 추위를 막는 기능이 중요한 옷에 어울려요. '방한복을 입다·챙기다'로 말해요.
explain_en: '겨울옷' is ordinary winter clothing, while 방한복 suits clothing whose cold-blocking function matters, such as for hiking, outdoor activities or work sites. You say '방한복을 입다' or '챙기다'.

examples.en: I trimmed the fine hair on my face with a razor.

examples.ko: 복숭아 껍질에는 잔털이 많이 나 있어요.
examples.en: Peach skin has a lot of fine fuzz on it.

examples.ko: 제 얼굴의 잔털은 햇빛에 금색으로 보여요.
examples.en: The fine hair on my face looks golden in the sunlight.

examples.ko: 아기는 이마와 볼에 잔털도 나 있어요.
examples.en: The baby has fine hair on the forehead and cheeks too.

examples.ko: 잔털 제거 크림을 써 봤는데 피부가 따가웠어요.
examples.en: I tried a hair removal cream, but my skin stung.
It was so scary that even the fine hairs on my neck stood up.

explain: '솜털'과 비슷하지만, '잔털'은 얼굴, 팔, 다리에 난 가늘고 짧은 털을 말할 때 폭넓게 써요. 굵고 진한 털은 그냥 '털'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is close to '솜털' (down), but 잔털 is used broadly for thin, short hairs on the face, arms and legs. Thick, dark hair is just called '털'.

examples.en: I sit cross-legged on the floor and eat.
If I sit cross-legged, my legs go numb.
The children sat in a circle with their legs crossed.
If sitting cross-legged is uncomfortable, sit on a chair.
I watched TV sitting cross-legged.

examples.ko: 명상할 때는 책상다리를 하고 허리를 펴요.
examples.en: When meditating, I sit cross-legged and straighten my back.

explain: 바닥에 앉아 두 다리를 꼬아 앞으로 모으는 자세예요. 보통 '책상다리를 하다'로 쓰고 '양반다리'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It is the sitting posture on the floor with your legs crossed in front of you. It is usually used as '책상다리를 하다', and people also call it '양반다리'.

examples.en: Her nose bridge is high, so her profile is pretty.
My nose bridge is low, so my glasses keep sliding down.
Wrinkles form on the bridge of my nose when I laugh.
I pushed my glasses up the bridge of my nose.

examples.ko: 새 마스크가 콧대를 꽉 눌러서 아파요.
examples.en: The new mask presses hard on my nose bridge and it hurts.
I made my nose bridge look higher with makeup.

explain: 코의 위쪽 길게 이어진 선에 써요. 콧구멍이나 코끝은 다른 말이에요. 안경, 마스크, 화장 이야기에 자주 나와요. 비유로도 쓰는 말이라서 아래 표현을 같이 보세요.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 인기가 많아서 콧대가 높아요.
phrases.en: be stuck-up; look down on others
phrases.nuance_ko: 잘난 척하고 다른 사람을 얕보는 태도를 말해요. 반대로 '콧대를 꺾다'는 잘난 척하는 사람의 기를 눌러 준다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a proud attitude of looking down on others. '콧대를 꺾다' means to take a boastful person down a peg.
phrases.en_equiv: have one's nose in the air

explain_en: It refers to the long upper line of the nose; the nostrils and the tip are different words. It comes up in talk about glasses, masks, and makeup. It is also used figuratively, so see the expression below.

en: be tangled; be entangled; be disheveled

examples.en: My hair got all messed up because of the wind.
My hair is always messy when I wake up.
The thread is so tangled that I can't undo it.

examples.ko: 헝클어진 머리로 학교에 갈 수는 없어요.
examples.en: I can't go to school with messy hair.

examples.ko: 방 안이 헝클어져 있어서 정리해야 해요.
examples.en: The room is a mess, so I need to tidy it up.

examples.ko: 서류가 헝클어지지 않게 파일에 꽂아 주세요.
examples.en: Please put the documents in a file so they don't get jumbled.

explain: 머리카락, 실, 끈처럼 길고 가는 것이 엉킬 때 가장 잘 어울려요. '흐트러지다'는 정돈된 것이 흩어질 때 쓰는 말이라 느낌이 조금 달라요. 사람이 일부러 그렇게 만들 때는 '머리를 헝클다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It fits best for long, thin things like hair, thread, or string that get tangled. '흐트러지다' is for something neat that scatters, so the feel is a little different. When a person does it on purpose, use the active verb, as in '머리를 헝클다'.
